answer: Default FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS is set to 0o644 in django/conf/global_settings.py

The model FilePathField already supports a callable `path`: `formfield()` resolves it with `self.path() if callable(self.path) else self.path`. `deconstruct()` stores the callable itself, so migrations keep the callable and not the resolved path.

The `ordering_parts` regex in `SQLCompiler` is the cause. Without `re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL`, `(.*)` stops at the first newline, so `search(sql)` matched only the last line of a multiline RawSQL. `get_order_by()` then added that last line to `seen` and dropped later clauses that ended the same way. The compiler now defines the regex as `r"^(.*)\s(?:ASC|DESC).*"` with `re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL`, so `(.*)` spans the whole multiline SQL. `get_order_by()` uses it at line 501 (`without_ordering = self.ordering_parts.search(sql)[1]`) to build the duplicate-detection key.

Fixed in Media.merge (django/forms/widgets.py), which uses a TopologicalSorter over all lists at once, with Media.__add__ just collecting the lists (_js_lists) rather than merging pairwise, so unnecessary order constraints are no longer imposed.

In sqlmigrate.py, self.output_transaction is assigned `migration.atomic and connection.features.can_rollback_ddl`, so BEGIN/COMMIT is only emitted when the migration is atomic and the database supports transactional DDL.
The DurationField invalid error message already uses the corrected format "[DD] [[HH:]MM:]ss[.uuuuuu]".

The trailing-newline bug is fixed in both username validators. ASCIIUsernameValidator.regex and UnicodeUsernameValidator.regex in django/contrib/auth/validators.py are r"^[\w.@+-]+\Z". The trailing `$` was replaced with `\Z`, so a username ending in a newline no longer matches. The leading anchor is still `^` rather than the `\A` the report suggested. That is equivalent here because the regexes don't use MULTILINE. The ASCII validator's regex is at line 10 and the Unicode validator's is at line 20. I only read the file; I didn't run the validators.

The fix is already in the code. `HttpResponseBase.make_bytes` in `corpus/django/http/response.py` checks `isinstance(value, (bytes, memoryview))` and returns `bytes(value)`. A `memoryview` therefore becomes its real bytes, not the `str()` form `b'<memory at 0x...>'`. The `content` setter also skips the iterable branch for `memoryview`, so it goes through `make_bytes` as a single value. I didn't run the example from the question.

In Collector.delete(), the fast-delete path for a single instance with no dependencies now clears the PK after the delete query runs, with setattr(instance, model._meta.pk.attname, None). This is the line the issue asked to add (it pointed at the old line 280).

The migration's update_proxy_model_permissions moves permissions from the concrete model's content type to the proxy's. If Permission rows already exist for the proxy content type, the update hits a unique-constraint IntegrityError. That is the case for models recreated as proxies. The code now wraps the update in transaction.atomic and catches IntegrityError. It prints a warning that tells you to audit the permissions, instead of crashing the migration.

The fix is in `iter_modules_and_files` in `django/utils/autoreload.py`. For `__main__` and `__mp_main__` (usually manage.py), it skips the `__spec__` check and appends `module.__file__` to the watched paths. The `__spec__` check would otherwise skip them, because `__main__` often has no `__spec__`. The `hasattr` guard covers cases where `__file__` is missing, such as running under ipdb.

Django already handles this in `LazySettings`. When `MEDIA_URL` or `STATIC_URL` is read, `__getattr__` calls `_add_script_prefix`. That method prepends the script prefix (`SCRIPT_NAME`) to relative values. It leaves values that start with `http://`, `https://` or `/` unchanged. The result is cached on the settings object.

The code suggests this is a known network-filesystem quirk: `iter_modules_and_files` in `autoreload.py` has a comment saying "Network filesystems may return null bytes in file paths." It catches the error, logs it at debug level, and skips that path instead of crashing. The exact call site in the report may differ, so this is inferred from the surrounding code rather than confirmed against the reported traceback.

An Http404 raised in a converter's to_python propagates out of resolve() before request.resolver_match is set. technical_404_response in corpus/django/views/debug.py handles that case at line 619: `tried = request.resolver_match.tried if request.resolver_match else None`. That line is the guard that lets the technical 404 response be built when there is no resolver_match. I picked this line from reading the code and recalling the upstream fix. I did not run anything to confirm it.

The models.E028 check is in `check_all_models` in django/core/checks/model_checks.py. It collects each managed, non-proxy model's `db_table` and reports an error when more than one model uses the same table name. When `settings.DATABASE_ROUTERS` is set, the same condition is reported as warning models.W035 instead of an error. So the check is intentional, and configuring DATABASE_ROUTERS for your multi-database setup turns it into a warning.

The check is in Field._check_choices in django/db/models/fields/__init__.py. It finds the longest choice value, including values inside grouped choices. If that length is greater than max_length, it returns the error fields.E009: "'max_length' is too small to fit the longest value in 'choices' (%d characters)." I read only lines 362–377 and relied on the ranked snippets for the rest. The line below is where the comparison and the error are raised.

The bug is in `Exact.get_prep_lookup` in `lookups.py`. For a sliced subquery, it clears the select clause and adds `pk` unless the subquery already has select fields. When that check misses, the `.values('m')` select is replaced by `id`, and the GROUP BY follows it, so `GROUP BY U0."email"` becomes `GROUP BY U0."id"`. The guard is line 337, `if not self.rhs.has_select_fields:`. `Query.set_values` sets `has_select_fields = True` at `query.py:2387`, so a `.values()` subquery should skip the override. I only read these lines and did not run the example.

EnumSerializer.serialize in django/db/migrations/serializer.py already emits enum members by name (e.g. `module.Status['GOOD']`) through `f"{module}.{enum_class.__qualname__}[{item.name!r}]"`. That is the fix the ticket asks for, so the code in this corpus is already fixed.

The two-digit year check in parse_http_date (django/utils/http.py) no longer hardcodes 0-69 as 2000-2069 and 70-99 as 1970-1999. It compares against the current year. If the two-digit year is more than 50 above the current year's last two digits, it is read as the previous century (`year += current_century - 100`). Otherwise it is read in the current century (`year += current_century`).
The `IsNull` lookup's `as_sql` raises `ValueError("The QuerySet value for an isnull lookup must be True or False.")` when the right-hand side is not a `bool`.

The autodetector's generate_altered_fields handles a ForeignKey whose to_field target was renamed. It looks up the rename in self.renamed_fields (via to_field_rename_key) and repoints new_field.remote_field.field_name to the old field's name for comparison. The block starts at line 1130.

Choices.__str__ in django/db/models/enums.py returns str(self.value). This is the fix: casting a TextChoices/IntegerChoices member to str gives its value ("first") and not "MyChoice.FIRST_CHOICE". I didn't open the file or run anything. The answer comes from the ranked snippet.
Field.contribute_to_class only sets the default get_FOO_display partialmethod if "get_%s_display" isn't already in cls.__dict__, so an explicitly defined override on the class is preserved.

The "database is locked" error comes from `test_db_signature()` in the SQLite backend's `creation.py`. It uses the alias to tell in-memory test databases apart, but for file-backed ones it only used the connection's `NAME`. Test databases with different `TEST["NAME"]` values could therefore be treated as the same database. The `else: sig.append(test_database_name)` branch at line 127 fixes this by adding the test database name to the signature. I did not run the test; this is from reading the code and from my recollection of the upstream fix.

The inner-class path bug is fixed in Field.deconstruct(). It builds the path from `self.__class__.__qualname__` instead of `__name__`, so an inner class is written as `Outer.Inner`. For classes passed as arguments (like the enum in the second example), `TypeSerializer` in db/migrations/serializer.py (line 183) also uses `__qualname__`.

The crash comes from `RegexPattern.match` in `django/urls/resolvers.py`. In the question's pattern, the outer `(?P<format>...)` group is named, but it contains an inner unnamed group `(html|json|xml)`. When the optional part doesn't match, `match.groups()` returns `(None, None)`, and those values get passed as positional args. The view then receives 3 positional arguments (request plus two Nones), which gives the `TypeError`.

Line 206 is `args = () if kwargs else match.groups()`. It is the fix for this: if there are any named groups, positional args are dropped. Line 207 then filters out kwargs whose value is `None`, so the view's default for `format` applies. I didn't run anything to confirm it. I read the code, which already contains this handling.

The code addresses this: `contribute_to_class` only skips installing `get_FOO_display` when the class's own `__dict__` defines it, so inherited methods don't block the child's version. The child's `get_FOO_display` is bound to the child's own field, whose `flatchoices` includes the new tuples, so `_get_FIELD_display` can return "output3" for "C".

The E004 check, `check_language_settings_consistent`, calls `get_supported_language_variant(settings.LANGUAGE_CODE)` and returns E004 only if that raises LookupError. That call is the base-language fallback: it tries `de-at`, then `de`. So a LANGUAGE_CODE like "de-at" no longer raises E004 when `de` is available. The repo already contains this fix, so I made no changes. I read the code but did not run it.

The special case for models.JSONField is in `display_for_field` in django/contrib/admin/utils.py. It serializes the value with json.dumps, using the field's encoder, so read-only values show as valid JSON. It falls back to `display_for_value` if a TypeError is raised.

The fix is already in the code. `BaseDatabaseCreation.deserialize_db_from_string` wraps the load in `atomic(using=self.connection.alias)`. Inside it, constraint checks are disabled while the objects are saved. `check_constraints` then runs on the affected tables, so forward references and cycles no longer cause integrity errors.

In SQLCompiler.find_ordering_name, a relation field (e.g. the parent_ptr that "pk" resolves to for a multi-table child) has the related model's default ordering appended, which loses the "-" direction for "-pk". The guard `name != "pk"` in the condition skips that expansion so the ordering on pk keeps its DESC direction.

The hint in the fields.E334 and fields.E335 checks in ManyToManyField._check_relationship_model now reads 'If you want to create a recursive relationship, use ManyToManyField("%s", through="%s").' It no longer says ForeignKey and no longer includes symmetrical=False. No "use ForeignKey(" text remains in the codebase.

In `Query.set_group_by`, a non-aggregate annotation is grouped by its alias: `group_by.append(Ref(alias, annotation))`. Here the alias is `status`, so the SQL gets `GROUP BY "status"`. `status` is also a real column on the joined `test_app_ab` table, so PostgreSQL reports the reference as ambiguous. Django 2.2 grouped by the full subquery expression, which avoids this. This line is the likely cause, but I haven't run the query or traced how the compiler renders the `Ref`.

The fix is already in `cleanse_setting()` in `corpus/django/views/debug.py`. It recurses into `dict`, `list` and `tuple` values. The `list` branch at line 136-137 calls `cleanse_setting("", v)` on each item, so dicts nested inside lists get their sensitive keys masked. The `tuple` branch at line 138-139 does the same. Before this, only `dict`s were cleansed and other iterables were returned as-is. I read the code but did not run it.

The crash comes from `_delete_composed_index()` in `django/db/backends/base/schema.py`. It raises `ValueError("Found wrong number (N) of constraints ...")` whenever `len(constraint_names) != 1`. With both a `unique_together` and an `index_together` on the same fields, the lookup for the index could match both the `_uniq` and the `_idx` constraint. In this checkout, `alter_index_together()` already guards against that. It passes `{"index": True, "unique": False}` when deleting an index, so the unique constraint is excluded and only the `_idx` one is left. That `unique: False` filter at line 598 is where the bug is handled. I only read the code and did not run a migration to confirm it.

In `Collector.delete()`, the fast-delete loop only adds a model's label to `deleted_counter` when its count is non-zero (`if count:`). Without that check, a "simple" model with no foreign keys would return `(0, {'my_app.BlockLibrary': 0})`. With it, a zero-row delete returns `(0, {})`, the same as models that have foreign keys. The loop that deletes instances has the same guard at lines 507-508.

One path still returns a zero entry. When there is a single object with no dependencies, line 457 returns `count, {model._meta.label: count}` directly. That only happens when there is one instance to delete, so its count is not zero in practice.

The check is in `Model._check_constraints` in django/db/models/base.py. It calls `cls._check_local_fields(fields, "constraints")`, and `_check_local_fields` raises models.E012 for fields that don't exist. This is the same check `unique_together` uses.
QuerySet.distinct() calls self._not_support_combined_queries("distinct"), so calling distinct() on a union queryset raises NotSupportedError.

StaticFilesHandlerMixin.get_response_async in django/contrib/staticfiles/handlers.py. It serves the request with sync_to_async(self.serve, thread_sensitive=False) and turns Http404 into a response with response_for_exception.
slugify() in django/utils/text.py now strips leading and trailing dashes and underscores. The fix is the final `.strip("-_")` applied after the `re.sub(r"[-\s]+", "-", value)` call.

The error comes from `Query.check_filterable()`. It raises NotSupportedError when the filter value has a `resolve_expression` attribute and `getattr(expression, "filterable", True)` is falsy. A model instance that has a field called `filterable` set to False, like the `ProductMetaDataType` in the report, is therefore rejected as if it were a non-filterable expression. The check is in the `if` at lines 1293-1295, and the `raise` follows it.

The default ordering of a related model gets applied in `find_ordering_name` in compiler.py. The condition there is `field.is_relation and opts.ordering and getattr(field, "attname", None) != pieces[-1] and name != "pk" and not has_transforms`. The `attname != pieces[-1]` check stops `order_by("record__root_id")` from picking up OneModel's `-id` ordering. It also stops the extra self-join. I'm answering from the ranked snippet. I read it, but I did not run the queryset.

Query.set_empty() now adds a NothingNode to the outer query's where clause and also calls set_empty() on each query in self.combined_queries. QuerySet.none() calls it, so none() on a union() empties every combined sub-query and returns no rows instead of all of them.

ValidationError.__eq__ is defined in django/core/exceptions.py. It returns NotImplemented for non-ValidationError objects. Otherwise it compares hash(self) == hash(other). __hash__ builds the hash from message, code and params for a single error. For an error_dict or error_list it hashes the contents, so the comparison doesn't depend on the order the errors were raised in. I read lines 195–234 and didn't read the rest of __hash__, so the order-independence for lists and dicts comes from the code ranking, not from reading it.

The `comments` argument is already passed to `feed.add_item()` in `Feed.get_feed()`, as `comments=self._get_dynamic_attr("item_comments", item)`. Subclasses can define `item_comments` directly, without going through `item_extra_kwargs`.

In generate_created_models, the autodetector emits AlterOrderWithRespectTo (which creates the `_order` field) before the AddIndex operations for the new model's indexes. The `# Generate other opns` block that adds AlterOrderWithRespectTo starts at line 702, and the `for index in indexes` loop that adds AddIndex comes after it at line 718. Your migration has AddIndex first, so it matches the order from before this fix.

The duplicate-options problem is handled in apply_limit_choices_to_to_formfield in django/forms/models.py. It no longer filters the queryset directly with limit_choices_to, because a join in that filter could return the same row more than once. It now wraps the filter in an Exists() subquery, which avoids the duplicates. The subquery runs on the model's _base_manager. It combines limit_choices_to (converted to a Q if needed) with Q(pk=OuterRef("pk")).

SessionBase.decode now catches any exception (including the binascii.Error "Incorrect padding" from legacy decoding) and returns an empty session dict instead of crashing. BadSignature is logged as "Session data corrupted". All other exceptions are swallowed in the `except Exception` clause.

Field.__eq__ in django/db/models/fields/__init__.py compares creation_counter and also getattr(self, "model", None), so fields on different models compare unequal. __lt__ (line 669) orders by creation_counter first and then by model. __hash__ (line 689) still hashes only creation_counter, so it was not adjusted to include the model. I read the code and did not run it.

The model class is added to each model's dict in the app_list context by `AdminSite._build_app_dict` in corpus/django/contrib/admin/sites.py, via the entry `"model": model`. This code already includes the change, so nothing needed fixing there. I didn't check whether `_build_app_dict` was also made public. It is still named `_build_app_dict` here, as the ranked snippets show.

The crash comes from `serialize_db_to_string()` in `django/db/backends/base/creation.py`. With `"TEST": {"MIGRATE": False}`, `create_test_db` sets `MIGRATION_MODULES` to None for every app, so `migrate` creates no tables for them. It then restores `MIGRATION_MODULES` in the `finally` block before serializing. `get_objects()` builds a fresh `MigrationLoader` after that restore, so its `migrated_apps` includes apps whose tables were never created. The check `app_config.label in loader.migrated_apps` therefore lets `django.contrib.admin` through, and querying `django_admin_log` raises `UndefinedTable`. This is a best guess from reading the code, not something I confirmed by running it or by finding the upstream fix. This copy of the code already contains that `migrated_apps` check, so I couldn't tell what the fix changed.

PasswordResetTokenGenerator._make_hash_value() now includes the user's email (via user.get_email_field_name(), empty string if missing) in the hash, so changing the email invalidates outstanding reset tokens.

The bug is fixed in Query.resolve_lookup_value. For namedtuples (types with `_make`), it now rebuilds the tuple with `type_(*values)`, which expands the resolved values. Other list and tuple types still get `type_(values)`.

ManagementUtility.execute now creates the pre-processing CommandParser with prog=self.prog_name (alongside usage="%(prog)s subcommand [options] [args]", add_help=False, allow_abbrev=False), so %(prog)s refers to the computed program name rather than sys.argv[0].

The crash comes from `exec()` in the shell command's `handle()`. It ran the `-c` code without an explicit globals dict, so functions defined in that code couldn't see names the code had imported. The code here already passes `globals()` to `exec`, which is the fix. The `-c` branch is `exec(options["command"], globals())`. The stdin branch at line 127 is the same fix.

InlineModelAdmin.__init__ in django/contrib/admin/options.py now derives verbose_name_plural from the Inline's verbose_name when only verbose_name is set. If neither is set, it uses the model's Meta verbose_name_plural. The fallback is `format_lazy("{}s", self.verbose_name)`.

KeyTransformIsNull in django/db/models/fields/json.py: as_oracle and as_sqlite must use the has-key logic for isnull=True as well (SQLite: JSON_TYPE(lhs, key) IS NULL; Oracle: NOT has_key OR lhs IS NULL) instead of the generic IsNull SQL, so JSON null values with the key present don't match.

Exceptions caught in Signal.send_robust() are now logged by the new helper method `_log_robust_failure`. It calls `logger.error("Error calling %s in Signal.send_robust() (%s)", ..., exc_info=err)`. The `except Exception as err` clauses in send_robust() and asend() call this helper.

The W042 check is `Model._check_default_pk` in `django/db/models/base.py`. It skips models whose auto-created pk is an inherited parent link: `isinstance(cls._meta.pk, OneToOneField) and cls._meta.pk.remote_field.parent_link`, with the comment "Inherited PKs are checked in parents models." The check only warns when `cls._meta.pk.auto_created` is true. The warning is meant for the model that actually creates the pk, which is the parent. It should not fire for children that inherit a manually specified pk.

I read this code but did not run it or test the reported case. The listed models may still warn if the pk really is auto-created in an ancestor, or if it isn't a parent-link `OneToOneField`.

ModelChoiceField.default_error_messages["invalid_choice"] is the message to change. It currently reads "Select a valid choice. That choice is not one of the available choices." and has no %(value)s placeholder. The fix is to change it to "Select a valid choice. %(value)s is not one of the available choices.", the same text ChoiceField and ModelMultipleChoiceField use. ModelChoiceField.to_python already passes params={"value": value} when it raises the ValidationError (models.py:1554-1558), so only the message text needs to change.

In Model._prepare_related_fields_for_save, the check `elif getattr(self, field.attname) in field.empty_values:` re-sets the related object after it has been saved. That copies the pk the related object got after the assignment, such as sku="foo", into product_id. The older code tested `is None`, so an empty-string pk was never refreshed.

Q._combine in django/db/models/query_utils.py used to deepcopy the other Q when `self` was empty, and that deepcopy is what raised "cannot pickle 'dict_keys' object". In this code it now returns `other.copy()`, a shallow copy that doesn't pickle the children. The fix is on line 59, `return other.copy()`. The related `if not other` branch on line 61 does the same with `self.copy()`.

The TypeError comes from `Q._combine` in `corpus/django/db/models/query_utils.py`. In the original code it rejected anything that wasn't a `Q`, via `if not isinstance(other, Q): raise TypeError(other)`. In this corpus the check is already relaxed to `getattr(other, "conditional", False) is False`. Conditional expressions such as `Exists` therefore pass, so `Q() & Exists(...)` no longer raises. The line that raises is line 57, `raise TypeError(other)`, inside the check on line 56. I did not add a `__rand__`, and I did not run the example.

ResolverMatch.__repr__ special-cases functools.partial. If self.func is a partial, it uses repr(self.func). Otherwise it uses self._func_path. __init__ doesn't unwrap partials. It sets self.func = func and computes _func_path from the un-unwrapped func.

The check is `AutoFieldMeta.__subclasscheck__` in `corpus/django/db/models/fields/__init__.py`. Its first clause is at line 2843. The `_subclasses` property at line 2835 returns `(BigAutoField, SmallAutoField)`. In this checkout the line already reads `issubclass(subclass, self._subclasses) or super().__subclasscheck__(subclass)`. That form accepts subclasses of `BigAutoField` and `SmallAutoField`, so the bug is already fixed here. The bug as reported would come from an exact-match test (`subclass in self._subclasses`) on that line. I didn't run anything to confirm.

The directory-name check for `startapp` is in `TemplateCommand.handle()` in `django/core/management/templates.py`, at line 106: `self.validate_name(os.path.basename(top_dir), "directory")`. The code in this checkout no longer has the bug. The old code called `basename()` on the raw `target`. A trailing slash made `basename()` return `''`, which `validate_name` rejected as "not a valid app directory". Line 104 now sets `top_dir = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(target))`, and `abspath` removes any trailing slash. `basename(top_dir)` therefore returns the real directory name. I didn't run `startapp` to confirm.
ReadOnlyPasswordHashWidget already overrides id_for_label() to return None, so BoundField.label_tag (boundfield.py:190-192) leaves out the 'for' attribute on its label.

BoundWidget.id_for_label in this codebase already returns the id set in the widget's attrs: `return self.data["attrs"].get("id")`. It no longer builds `'id_%s_%s'` from name and index, so the fix the issue asks for is in place.

The bug is in `TypeSerializer` in `django/db/migrations/serializer.py`. Its special case for `models.Model` serializes to the string "models.Model" and carries the import `from django.db import models`. I found this by searching the code and did not run the reproduction.

FormSets already add the "nonform" CSS class to non-form errors. full_clean() creates `self._non_form_errors` with `error_class="nonform"`, and the ValidationError handler later in full_clean() does the same.

Query.add_deferred_loading in corpus/django/db/models/sql/query.py handles defer() after only(). When the names left after removing the deferred ones are empty, it calls clear_deferred_loading() and then sets the new deferred set. This code already looks like the upstream fix. I read it and did not run the queries from the report.
ManyToManyRel.identity wraps self.through_fields in make_hashable(...), so a list value no longer makes the hash fail. The code you pasted already has this fix.

ManyToManyField's system check emits warning fields.W345 ("related_name has no effect on ManyToManyField with a symmetrical relationship, e.g. to "self".") when `self.remote_field.symmetrical and self._related_name`. It is a check warning, not a raised error.

The refactor is already in the code. AutocompleteJsonView.get() builds the results with `self.serialize_result(obj, to_field_name)`. The new `serialize_result()` method returns `{"id": str(getattr(obj, to_field_name)), "text": str(obj)}`. Subclasses can override it to add extra fields, such as `notes`, without rewriting get().

In `_multi_decorate`, the bound method is wrapped in a `partial`, which has no `__name__` or `__module__`. The fix is `bound_method = wraps(method)(partial(method.__get__(self, type(self))))`. `wraps(method)` copies the original method's attributes onto the partial before the decorators are applied.

The fix is already in `get_admin_url` in `django/contrib/admin/helpers.py`. The `reverse()` call passes `current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name`, so readonly ForeignKey links resolve under the current admin site (for example `/custom-admin/...`) and not the default `/admin/...`. I didn't run the test suite.

ModelChoiceIteratorValue lacked a __hash__ method, so using it as a dict key or in a dict lookup raised "unhashable type". The fix is to define `__hash__` on the class as `return hash(self.value)`. It sits alongside the existing `__eq__`, which defining `__eq__` alone had made unhashable.

The "." operator error comes from the index expressions being resolved with table-qualified columns. In this codebase, `UniqueConstraint._get_index_expressions` resolves them against `Query(model, alias_cols=False)`. That makes the `F('name')` and `F('value')` expressions compile to bare column names. SQLite rejects qualified names in index expressions, so this is the line that avoids the error. I didn't reproduce the crash or run any code.

`_create_unique_sql` in `base/schema.py` also builds its compiler with `alias_cols=False`. `_remake_table` in `sqlite3/schema.py` only copies `model._meta.constraints` into the new model.

The fix belongs in `RenameModel.database_forwards` in `corpus/django/db/migrations/operations/models.py`. I haven't changed any code or run anything. That method is where the rename work happens, and it has no check for an unchanged table name. If a model sets `db_table`, renaming the model leaves the old and new table names identical. The method should then return early and skip the whole body. Today it goes on to alter the related fields pointing at the model, which is what drops and recreates foreign keys on Postgres and rebuilds the table on SQLite. `alter_db_table` in `base/schema.py` already skips the table rename itself when the names match, but that doesn't stop the related-field loop. The guard should compare `old_model._meta.db_table` with `new_model._meta.db_table` and sit inside the `allow_migrate_model` check at line 437.

MultiWidget.id_for_label is defined in corpus/django/forms/widgets.py at line 937. It currently returns "" (`return ""`), so it adds no "_0" index and renders no `for` attribute. The ticket asks to remove this method from MultiWidget entirely.

URLValidator.__call__ in django/core/validators.py catches the ValueError that urlsplit raises and re-raises it as a ValidationError. The traceback's urlsplit call at validators.py line 130 is this one. forms.URLField.to_python does the same through its split_url helper.

The empty `SELECT AS "foo"` comes from the compiler's `get_select()`. `~Q(pk__in=[])` compiles to a WHERE node that matches everything, so compiling it raises `FullResultSet`. This checkout already has the fix: `get_select()` catches `FullResultSet` and compiles `Value(True)`, so the annotation selects a true value instead of empty SQL. I did not run the example to confirm it.

`EmptyResultSet` is handled just above it by selecting `0`, which is why `ExpressionWrapper(Q(pk__in=[]))` already worked.

MigrationRecorder.ensure_schema() creates the django_migrations table without consulting the db router's allow_migrate. record_applied() and record_unapplied() both call ensure_schema(), so migrate creates the table on every connection. applied_migrations() only checks has_table() and doesn't consult the router either. The fix belongs in ensure_schema(), or in the recorder methods that call it.

The fix is in the Subquery constructor: `self.query.subquery = True` (corpus/django/db/models/expressions.py), so as_sql()'s `subquery_sql[1:-1]` strips the parentheses added by the query rather than real characters.
MessageEncoder.default in cookie.py checks `if obj.extra_tags is not None:` before appending extra_tags. This is the fix, so an empty-string extra_tags is now serialized and not turned into None.

The template autoreloader's `template_changed` handler treats any changed file under a template directory as a template change. With BASE_DIR in DIRS, that covers every project file, including .py files. The handler resets the loaders and returns True, which tells the autoreloader the change was handled, so the server doesn't restart. The guard that skips .py files and returns None, so the normal restart still happens, is at `if file_path.suffix == ".py": return`. I did not run the repro.

SimpleLazyObject doesn't implement __radd__ in the original report, but this code does. `LazyObject` in django/utils/functional.py defines it with the `new_method_proxy` decorator: `def __radd__(self, other): return other + self`. `new_method_proxy` first sets up the wrapped object if it is still `empty`. It then calls the function with the wrapped object as `self`, so the addition runs on the real object. `SimpleLazyObject` subclasses `LazyObject`, so it inherits this.

Empty If-Modified-Since is ignored in get_conditional_response: `if_modified_since and parse_http_date_safe(if_modified_since)` leaves an empty string falsy, so the header is skipped instead of raising an exception.

RenameIndex.database_backwards() in django/db/migrations/operations/models.py returns early (a no-op) when old_fields is set, i.e. for an unnamed index. The auto-generated name is never restored. Re-applying database_forwards() then tries to rename to a name that already exists, which causes the crash. The fix is to remove that early return and restore the old auto-generated name.

The fix is in `AlterTogetherOptionOperation.references_field`. It treats an `AlterUniqueTogether` with an empty value as referencing every field of the model (`not self.option_value`). That stops the optimizer from moving the unique_together removal past the field removal. I did not reproduce the error or run a migration to confirm this.

The autodetector already emits the removal first. `generate_removed_altered_unique_together` runs before `generate_removed_fields` (autodetector.py:192 and 195). So the ordering there is correct. The `ValueError` itself is raised from `_delete_composed_index` in schema.py, which `alter_unique_together` calls.

Management command help is formatted by `DjangoHelpFormatter`, which is set as the default `formatter_class` in `BaseCommand.create_parser()`. It is a subclass of argparse's `HelpFormatter`, which re-wraps the description text. That re-wrapping collapses the newlines and indentation in `help`. `create_parser()` uses `kwargs.setdefault("formatter_class", DjangoHelpFormatter)`, so a command can pass its own formatter through `kwargs`. The class itself is defined at base.py:115. I read the code but did not run it or test a fix.

json_script() in django/utils/html.py now takes an optional `encoder` parameter: `def json_script(value, element_id=None, encoder=None)`. It serializes with `json.dumps(value, cls=encoder or DjangoJSONEncoder)`, so DjangoJSONEncoder is the default when no encoder is passed.

The check collects module paths per library name in `libraries = defaultdict(set)`. The same path can be added from both `TEMPLATES['OPTIONS']['libraries']` (lines 55-58) and the installed-app scan `get_template_tag_modules()` (lines 60-61). Because the values are a set, duplicates collapse, so `len(items) > 1` only fires for genuinely different paths. A list would report the same path twice, which matches the error you saw. The file already uses a set, so this check no longer produces that false positive. I didn't run it to confirm.

The fix is already in this codebase. `_get_only_select_mask` in `django/db/models/sql/query.py` now uses `field.remote_field.model._meta.concrete_model` for the related model, not the proxy model's own `_meta`. The select mask therefore includes the concrete model's pk, which avoids the `ValueError: 'id' is not in list`. This is the change the reporter suggested. `_get_defer_select_mask` has the same change at line 746. I didn't run the reproduction.

In inspectdb.py's handle_inspection, related_name is only added for 2nd+ relations to the same model (`if rel_to in used_relations:`), leaving the first relation without related_name, so reverse accessor clashes can still occur. The fix belongs in this block.

In PostgreSQL's DatabaseClient.settings_to_cmd_args_env, the extra parameters (`args.extend(parameters)`) are added before the dbname (`args += [dbname]`). This puts psql options ahead of the database name, so psql no longer ignores them.

EnumSerializer.serialize in django/db/migrations/serializer.py handles combined Enum flags. For an enum.Flag, it decomposes the value into its member flags. It uses list(self.value) on Python 3.11+ and enum._decompose otherwise. It then joins the members' names with " | ", producing e.g. re.RegexFlag['IGNORECASE'] | re.RegexFlag['UNICODE'].

`BaseFormSet.empty_form` in `corpus/django/forms/formsets.py` builds its kwargs with `**self.get_form_kwargs(None)` first. It then sets `"empty_permitted": True` and `"use_required_attribute": False` after that. Because the forced values come later in the dict, they override any `empty_permitted` the user put in `form_kwargs`. This means `empty_form` ignores a user-supplied `empty_permitted`, which is the expected behavior from the issue. I didn't run the reproduction. I only read this code, which already has the override in place.

The IndexError comes from `str_number[0]` in `numberformat.py`. When the value is null or an empty string, `str_number` is empty, so indexing `[0]` fails. The fix is to use `str_number.startswith("-")` or check `str_number and str_number[0] == "-"`.

UserChangeForm.__init__ in django/contrib/auth/forms.py formats the password help_text link as f"../../{self.instance.pk}/password/" instead of the hardcoded "../password/", so the password-change link works when UserAdmin is reached via to_field.

Field.formfield() in django/db/models/fields/__init__.py sets show_hidden_initial=True when the model field's default is callable. That adds the hidden "initial-..." input, which the ArrayField inline in the question renders. I did not confirm this is the exact line the upstream fix changed.

Fixed in Sitemap.get_latest_lastmod by passing default=None to max(), so an empty items() list returns None instead of raising ValueError: `return max([self.lastmod(item) for item in self.items()], default=None)`

FileBasedCache.has_key in filebased.py already has the fix. It no longer calls os.path.exists() before open(). It opens the file directly inside a try block and catches FileNotFoundError, returning False. That removes the window between the check and the open, so a file deleted by another thread (or by _is_expired) no longer raises.

The fix is in create_permissions (django/contrib/auth/management/__init__.py): the ContentType lookup uses ContentType.objects.db_manager(using).get_for_model(...) so the content type is looked up in the database passed to migrate, rather than going through the router's db_for_read.

The wrong object comes from the `local_setter` that `get_related_selections` assigns to a filtered relation in `compiler.py`. The code only uses `local_setter` when `len(joins) <= 2`. Otherwise it uses `local_setter_noop`. I did not run the test case, so I haven't confirmed that this guard makes it pass.

The `join` filter in `corpus/django/template/defaultfilters.py` (lines 594-604) already has the fix, so I made no edit. It takes `autoescape` and branches on it. With autoescape on, it escapes both the joining string and the items (line 599). With autoescape off, it runs `arg.join(value)` (line 601) and does not escape the joining string. The bug in the question was that the joining string was always run through `conditional_escape`, whatever `autoescape` said. I did not run the test case from the question.

In Query._get_only_select_mask, `related_model = field.remote_field.model._meta.concrete_model` picks the wrong model for reverse relations (it needs `field.related_model` when `field in opts.related_objects`), so the nested only() mask for the reverse OneToOne isn't applied to the related model's fields.

In this checkout, `QuerySet._batched_insert` already keeps `returning_fields` when `on_conflict == OnConflict.UPDATE`. The bug is in FunctionTypeSerializer.serialize in django/db/migrations/serializer.py. For a classmethod, it builds the path from `klass.__name__`. That gives only the innermost class name, `Capability`, so the nested class's outer class `Profile` is dropped. It should use `klass.__qualname__` instead, which gives `appname.models.Profile.Capability.default`.
